technical_body.purpose: AP announces itself. Timestamp, beacon interval, capability info, then IEs (SSID, DS Parameter Set, TIM, Country, RSN, HT/VHT/HE/EHT Cap, WPS, Vendor-Specific).
wctf_uses: IE stego (Vendor-Specific)
hidden SSID (null SSID IE)

fields.name: Timestamp
fields.notes: AP's TSF timer (microseconds since AP boot)

fields.name: Beacon Interval
fields.notes: TU count between beacons; typically 100 TU (102.4 ms)

fields.name: Information Elements
fields.notes: variable — SSID (0), Supported Rates (1), DS Parameter (3), TIM (5), Country (7), RSN (48), HT/VHT/HE/EHT Cap, WPS (221), Vendor-Specific (221). See ies.json for byte layouts.

technical_body.purpose: Client asks 'who's on this channel'. Carries preferred SSIDs → KARMA/MANA input; probe-IE order fingerprints the client.

client fingerprinting

fields.name: MAC Header
fields.notes: type=0, subtype=4; SA=STA, DA=broadcast or target BSSID

fields.name: Information Elements
fields.notes: SSID (0), Supported Rates (1), Extended Supported Rates (50), HT Cap (45), Extended Cap (127), Vendor-Specific (221). Client-fingerprint IE order matters.

technical_body.purpose: AP's response — same IEs as beacon, but unicast.

technical_body.purpose: 802.11w SA Query. AP challenges a client (or STA challenges AP) after receiving a suspicious deauth/disassoc when PMF is optional/required — response confirms the peer holds the current SA. Central to PMF integrity: if a spoofed deauth arrives and PMF is required, the recipient MUST send an SA Query and refuse to disassociate unless it gets an SA Query Response with a matching transaction ID.

fields.name: Transaction Identifier
fields.notes: opaque 2-byte cookie the responder must echo

wctf_uses: SA Query is a PMF-required detection surface — a WIDS can watch for an unusual burst of unanswered SA Query requests during a deauth flood, revealing an in-progress PMF-bypass attempt
